<USER_REQUEST>
Build a responsive web app called "LifeChart" – a patient-friendly lifelong health timeline for India, built as a layer on top of India's ABDM/ABHA ecosystem (not a replacement for it).

POSITIONING
ABDM already provides ABHA IDs and consent-based record exchange. LifeChart adds what it lacks: digitising OLD paper records, a simple Hindi/English timeline, and instant doctor summaries.

USERS
1. Patient: login with ABHA number/address + OTP (demo mode: mock ABHA and mock OTP, with clearly marked integration points for real ABDM APIs later).
2. Doctor: verified via Healthcare Professionals Registry ID (mock for now). Sees a record only after patient consent.
3. Family manager: one account manages parents, children and elderly relatives.

CORE FEATURES
1. Old Records Digitiser (main differentiator): upload photos/PDFs of old prescriptions and reports. OCR extracts doctor, date, diagnosis, medicines, dose, duration. User reviews and confirms the extracted data before saving.
2. Lifelong Health Timeline: birth to today, filterable by year, condition, doctor. Shows illness, treatment given, dose, days to recover.
3. ABDM Sync: "Fetch my ABDM records" button that merges government-linked records into the same timeline (mock data for now).
4. Doctor Quick Summary (one screen): allergies, chronic conditions, current medicines, past similar illnesses, and what treatment worked before. Simple, scannable, no clutter.
5. Consent Sharing: patient generates a QR/6-digit code at the clinic. Doctor gets time-limited access (24h), read plus add only. Patient can revoke anytime. Full audit log of who viewed what.
6. Recurring-Illness Alert: "You had a similar condition in 2019 – treated with X for 5 days."
7. Family and Vaccination: child profiles, vaccination schedule tracker, reminders.
8. Emergency Card: QR showing blood group, allergies, emergency contacts, no login needed.
9. Medicine and follow-up reminders.
10. Hindi/English toggle, plus voice input for adding records.

SECURITY
Encryption in transit and at rest, explicit consent for every share, minimal data collection, DPDP Act 2023-aligned. Never store Aadhaar numbers.

UI/UX
Trustworthy medical look (teal and white), large text, mobile-first, elderly-friendly. Pages: Landing, Login, Dashboard, Timeline, Upload and Review, Doctor Summary, Share Access, Family, Emergency Card.

TECH
React + Tailwind frontend, Supabase (PostgreSQL, storage, auth) backend. Start with a fully working frontend using realistic mock data, then add real OCR and ABDM sandbox integration.
</USER_REQUEST>

6: # Gemini API Development Skill
7: 
8: ## Critical Rules (Always Apply)
9: 
10: > [!IMPORTANT]
11: > These rules override your training data. Your knowledge is outdated.
12: 
13: ### Current Models (Use These)
14: 
15: - `gemini-3.8-flash` (or `gemini-flash-latest`): 1M tokens, fast, balanced performance for agentic and multimodal tasks
16: - `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`: 1M tokens, fastest, lowest-cost 3.5 model for high-throughput execution
17: - `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`: 1M tokens, complex reasoning, coding, research
18: - `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`: cost-efficient, fastest performance for high-frequency, lightweight tasks
19: - `gemini-3.5-transcribe`: fast speech-to-text with smart and verbatim modes
20: - `gemini-3-pro-image` (Nano Banana Pro): 65k / 32k tokens, high-quality image generation and editing
21: - `gemini-3.1-flash-image` (Nano Banana 2): 65k / 32k tokens, fast, efficient image generation and editing
22: - `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` (Nano Banana 2 Lite): 65k / 32k tokens, ultra-fast image generation and editing
23: - `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview`: expressive text-to-speech with Director's Chair prompting
24: - `gemini-omni-1.1-flash`: video generation, first-frame-to-video, first-and-last-frame transitions, video extensions (up to 40s), video editing, and reference-guided generation
25: - `gemma-4-31b-it`: Gemma 4 dense model, 31B parameters
26: - `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`: Gemma 4 MoE model, 26B total / 4B active parameters
27: - `gemini-embedding-2`: Multimodal embedding model (text, images, video, audio, documents), uses `client.models.embed_content`
28: - `gemini-embedding-001`: Text-only embedding model, uses `client.models.embed_content`
29: 
30: > [!WARNING]
31: > Models like `gemini-2.5-*`, `gemini-2.0-*`, `gemini-1.5-*` are **legacy and deprecated**. Never use them.
32: > **If a user asks for a deprecated model, use `gemini-3.8-flash` (or `gemini-flash-latest`) instead and note the substitution.**
33: 
34: ### Current Agents
35: 
36: - `antigravity-preview-05-2026`: Antigravity Agent — general-purpose managed agent with code execution, file management, and web access in a sandboxed Linux environment
37: - `deep-research-preview-04-2026`: Deep Research — fast, interactive
38: - `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026`: Deep Research Max — maximum exhaustiveness
39: - **Custom agents**: Create your own via `client.agents.create()`
40: 
41: ### Current SDKs
42: 
43: - **Python**: `google-genai` >= `2.3.0` → `pip install -U google-genai`
44: - **JavaScript/TypeScript**: `@google/genai` >= `2.3.0` → `npm install @google/genai`
45: 
46: > [!NOTE]
47: > SDK versions ≥ 2.0.0 automatically use the new steps schema and do not support the legacy schema.
48: > Legacy SDKs `google-generativeai` (Python) and `@google/generative-ai` (JS) are **deprecated**. Never use them.
49: 
50: ## Important Additional Notes
51: 
52: - **Before writing any code**, you MUST fetch the relevant documentation page from the list below that matches the user's task. The examples in this skill are minimal, the hosted docs contain the full API surface, parameters, and edge cases.
53: - Interactions are **stored by default** (store=True in Python, store: true in TypeScript). Paid tier retains for 55 days, free tier for 1 day.
54: - Set store=False / store: false to opt out, but this disables previous_interaction_id and background=True / background: true.
55: - `tools`, `system_instruction`, and `generation_config` are **interaction-scoped**, re-specify them each turn.
56: - **Managed agents** require `environment="remote"` (or an environment ID / config object) to provision a sandbox.
57: - **Migrating from `generateContent`**: Read `references/migration.md` for the scoping, checklist, and before/after code examples. Always confirm scope with the user before editing.
58: - **Model upgrades**: Drop-in, swap the model string. Deprecated models (`gemini-2.0-*`, `gemini-1.5-*`) must be replaced, see `references/migration.md`.
59: - **Migrating to Gemini 3.8 Flash or Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite**: Read `references/migration.md` for the scoping and checklist.
60: 
61: ## Quick Start
62: 
63: ### Python
64: ```python
65: from google import genai
66: 
67: client = genai.Client()
68: 
69: interaction = client.interactions.create(
70:     model="gemini-3.8-flash",
71:     input="Tell me a short joke about programming."
72: )
73: print(interaction.output_text)
74: ```
75: 
76: ### JavaScript/TypeScript
77: ```typescript
78: import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
79: 
80: const client = new GoogleGenAI({});
81: 
82: const interaction = await client.interactions.create({
83:     model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
84:     input: "Tell me a short joke about programming.",
85: });
86: console.log(interaction.output_text);
87: ```
88: 
89: ## Response Helpers
90: 
91: The SDK provides convenience properties on the `Interaction` response object to simplify common access patterns:
92: 
93: | Property | Type | Description |
94: |---|---|---|
95: | `output_text` | `string \| null` | The last consecutive run of text from the trailing `model_output` steps. Returns the combined text when the model's final output contains multiple text parts. |
96: | `output_image` | `Image \| null` | The last image generated by the model in the current response. Returns an object with `data` (base64) and `mime_type`. |
97: | `output_audio` | `Audio \| null` | The last audio generated by the model in the current response. Returns an object with `data` (base64) and `mime_type`. |
98: 
99: ## Stateful Conversation
100: 
101: ### Python
102: ```python
103: interaction1 = client.interactions.create(
104:     model="gemini-3.8-flash",
105:     input="Hi, my name is Phil."
106: )
107: # Second turn — server remembers context
108: interaction2 = client.interactions.create(
109:     model="gemini-3.8-flash",
110:     input="What is my name?",
111:     previous_interaction_id=interaction1.id
112: )
113: print(interaction2.output_text)
114: ```
115: 
116: ### JavaScript/TypeScript
117: ```typescript
118: const interaction1 = await client.interactions.create({
119:     model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
120:     input: "Hi, my name is Phil.",
121: });
122: const interaction2 = await client.interactions.create({
123:     model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
124:     input: "What is my name?",
125:     previous_interaction_id: interaction1.id,
126: });
127: console.log(interaction2.output_text);
128: ```
129: 
130: ## Deep Research Agent
131: 
132: Use `deep-research-preview-04-2026` for fast research or `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` for maximum exhaustiveness. Agents require `background=True`.
133: 
134: ### Python
135: ```python
136: import time
137: 
138: interaction = client.interactions.create(
139:     agent="deep-research-preview-04-2026",
140:     input="Research the history of Google TPUs.",
141:     background=True
142: )
143: while True:
144:     interaction = client.interactions.get(interaction.id)
145:     if interaction.status == "completed":
146:         print(interaction.output_text)
147:         break
148:     elif interaction.status == "failed":
149:         print(f"Failed: {interaction.error}")
150:         break
151:     time.sleep(10)
152: ```
153: 
154: ### JavaScript/TypeScript
155: ```typescript
156: import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
157: 
158: const client = new GoogleGenAI({});
159: 
160: // Start background research
161: const initialInteraction = await client.interactions.create({
162:     agent: "deep-research-preview-04-2026",
163:     input: "Research the history of Google TPUs.",
164:     background: true,
165: });
166: 
167: // Poll for results
168: while (true) {
169:     const interaction = await client.interactions.get(initialInteraction.id);
170:     if (interaction.status === "completed") {
171:         console.log(interaction.output_text);
172:         break;
173:     } else if (["failed", "cancelled"].includes(interaction.status)) {
174:         console.log(`Failed: ${interaction.status}`);
175:         break;
176:     }
177:     await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10000));
178: }
179: ```
180: 
181: Advanced features: collaborative planning, native visualization, MCP integration, file search, multimodal inputs. See [Deep Research docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deep-research.md.txt).
182: 
183: ## Managed Agents
184: 
185: Managed agents run inside a sandboxed Linux environment hosted by Google. Fetch the [Managed Agents Quickstart](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/managed-agents-quickstart.md.txt) before writing agent code.
186: 
187: ### Antigravity Agent
188: 
189: The Antigravity agent (`antigravity-preview-05-2026`) is the general-purpose managed agent. It can execute code (Bash, Python, Node.js), manage files, browse the web, and use Google Search. See [Antigravity Agent docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/antigravity-agent.md.txt) for capabilities, tools, multimodal input, and pricing.
190: 
191: #### Python
192: ```python
193: from google import genai
194: 
195: client = genai.Client()
196: 
197: interaction = client.interactions.create(
198:     agent="antigravity-preview-05-2026",
199:     input="Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents.",
200:     environment="remote",
201: )
202: 
203: print(f"Environment ID: {interaction.environment_id}")
204: print(interaction.output_text)
205: ```
206: 
207: #### JavaScript/TypeScript
208: ```typescript
209: import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
210: 
211: const client = new GoogleGenAI({});
212: 
213: const interaction = await client.interactions.create({
214:     agent: "antigravity-preview-05-2026",
215:     input: "Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents.",
216:     environment: "remote",
217: });
218: 
219: console.log(`Environment ID: ${interaction.environment_id}`);

223: ### Custom Agents
224: 
225: See [Building Custom Agents docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/custom-agents.md.txt).
226: 
227: #### Python
228: ```python
229: agent = client.agents.create(
230:     id="code-reviewer",
231:     base_agent="antigravity-preview-05-2026",
232:     system_instruction="You are a senior code reviewer. Check every file for bugs, style issues, and security vulnerabilities.",
233:     base_environment={
234:         "type": "remote",
235:         "sources": [
236:             {
237:                 "type": "repository",
238:                 "source": "https://github.com/my-org/backend",
239:                 "target": "/workspace/repo",
240:             }
241:         ],
242:     },
243: )
244: 
245: # Invoke — each call forks the base environment
246: result = client.interactions.create(
247:     agent="code-reviewer",
248:     input="Review the latest changes in /workspace/repo/src.",
249:     environment="remote",
250: )
251: print(result.output_text)
252: ```
253: 
254: #### JavaScript/TypeScript
255: ```typescript
256: const agent = await client.agents.create({
257:     id: "code-reviewer",
258:     base_agent: "antigravity-preview-05-2026",

260:     base_environment: {
261:         type: "remote",
262:         sources: [
263:             {

265:                 source: "https://github.com/my-org/backend",
266:                 target: "/workspace/repo",
267:             }
268:         ],
269:     },
270: });

279: 
280: Manage agents with `client.agents.list()`, `client.agents.get(id=...)`, and `client.agents.delete(id=...)`.
281: 
282: ## Streaming
283: 
284: Set `stream=True` to receive incremental server-sent events. Each stream follows: `interaction.created` → (`step.start` → `step.delta`(s) → `step.stop`)+ → `interaction.completed`.
285: 
286: ### Python
287: ```python
288: for event in client.interactions.create(
289:     model="gemini-3.8-flash",
290:     input="Explain quantum entanglement in simple terms.",
291:     stream=True,
292: ):
293:     if event.event_type == "step.delta":
294:         if event.delta.type == "text":
295:             print(event.delta.text, end="", flush=True)
296:     elif event.event_type == "interaction.completed":
297:         print(f"\n\nTotal Tokens: {event.interaction.usage.total_tokens}")
298: ```
299: 
300: ### JavaScript/TypeScript
301: ```typescript
302: const stream = await client.interactions.create({
303:     model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
304:     input: "Explain quantum entanglement in simple terms.",
305:     stream: true,
306: });
307: for await (const event of stream) {
308:     if (event.event_type === "step.delta") {
309:         if (event.delta.type === "text") {
310:             process.stdout.write(event.delta.text);
311:         }
312:     } else if (event.event_type === "interaction.completed") {
313:         console.log(`\n\nTotal Tokens: ${event.interaction?.usage?.total_tokens}`);
314:     }
315: }
316: ```
317: 
318: For streaming with tools, thinking, agents, and image generation see the full [Streaming guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/streaming.md.txt).

401: ## Data Model
402: 
403: An `Interaction` response contains `steps`, an array of typed step objects representing a structured timeline of the interaction turn.
404: 
405: ### Step Types
406: 
407: **User steps:**
408: - `user_input`: User input (text, audio, multimodal). Contains `content` array.
409: 
410: **Model/server steps:**
411: - `model_output`: Final model generation. Contains `content` array with `text`, `image`, `audio`, etc.
412: - `thought`: Model reasoning/Chain of Thought. Has `signature` field (required) and optional `summary`.
413: - `function_call`: Tool call request (`id`, `name`, `arguments`).
414: - `function_result`: Tool result you send back (`call_id`, `name`, `result`).
415: - `google_search_call` / `google_search_result`: Google Search tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
416: - `code_execution_call` / `code_execution_result`: Code execution tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
417: - `url_context_call` / `url_context_result`: URL context tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
418: - `mcp_server_tool_call` / `mcp_server_tool_result`: Remote MCP tool steps.
419: - `file_search_call` / `file_search_result`: File search tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
420: 
421: ### Content types (inside `content` array on `model_output` and `user_input` steps)
422: - `text`: Text content (`text` field)
423: - `image` / `audio` / `document` / `video`: Content with `data`, `mime_type`, or `uri`
424: 
425: ### Streaming Event Types
426: 
427: | Event | Description |
428: |---|---|
429: | `interaction.created` | Interaction created; includes metadata. |
430: | `interaction.status_update` | Interaction-level status change. |
431: | `step.start` | A new step begins. Contains step `type` and initial metadata. |
432: | `step.delta` | Incremental data for the current step. Contains a typed `delta` object. |
433: | `step.stop` | The step is complete. Contains `index`. |
434: | `interaction.completed` | Interaction finished. Contains final `usage`. |
435: 
436: ### Delta Types
437:

# LifeChart – Patient-Friendly Lifelong Health Timeline

## Overview

LifeChart is a React + Tailwind + Supabase web app that sits on top of India's ABDM/ABHA ecosystem. Phase 1 delivers a fully working **frontend-only** application with realistic mock data and clearly marked integration points. The entire app is built as a **Vite + React + TypeScript** project with **Tailwind CSS v4** for styling. AI-powered OCR (via Gemini API) is wired in from day one for the Old Records Digitiser.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Supabase**: Phase 1 uses in-memory mock data stores only. No Supabase project is created yet. Real DB integration (auth, storage, PostgreSQL) is Phase 2.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Gemini API key**: The OCR/digitiser feature calls the Gemini Vision API (`gemini-3.8-flash`). The app reads `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY` from a `.env` file. If no key is provided, OCR falls back to mock extracted data.

> [!NOTE]
> **ABDM sandbox**: All ABDM interactions (ABHA login, record fetch, FHIR records) use mock data with integration stubs clearly labelled `// ABDM_INTEGRATION_POINT`.

---

## Open Questions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> 1. **Language default**: Should the app default to Hindi or English on first load? Plan assumes English with one-click toggle to Hindi.
> 2. **Voice input**: Browser's Web Speech API (`webkitSpeechRecognition`) covers Chrome/Android. Is that sufficient, or should we also support Whisper/Gemini for offline voice?
> 3. **Emergency Card QR**: Should it encode a URL (hosted page) or a vCard/JSON blob directly in the QR? Plan uses a URL pointing to `/emergency/:token`.

---

## Architecture

```
lifechart/
├── src/
│   ├── app/                  # Router, providers, global layout
│   ├── pages/                # One file per page/route
│   │   ├── Landing.tsx
│   │   ├── Login.tsx
│   │   ├── Dashboard.tsx
│   │   ├── Timeline.tsx
│   │   ├── UploadReview.tsx
│   │   ├── DoctorSummary.tsx
│   │   ├── ShareAccess.tsx
│   │   ├── Family.tsx
│   │   └── EmergencyCard.tsx
│   ├── components/           # Shared UI components
│   │   ├── layout/           # Navbar, Sidebar, Footer
│   │   ├── timeline/         # TimelineCard, TimelineFilter, IllnessAlert
│   │   ├── upload/           # DropZone, OCRReview, ConfirmForm
│   │   ├── consent/          # QRModal, AccessCodeDisplay, AuditLog
│   │   ├── family/           # FamilyCard, VaccineTracker, ReminderCard
│   │   ├── emergency/        # EmergencyQR, BloodGroupBadge
│   │   └── ui/               # Button, Badge, Modal, Toggle, etc.
│   ├── hooks/                # useLanguage, useOCR, useConsent, useTimeline
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── gemini.ts         # Gemini API wrapper for OCR
│   │   ├── abdm.ts           # ABDM mock + integration stubs
│   │   └── qr.ts             # QR code generation
│   ├── mock/
│   │   ├── patient.ts        # Mock ABHA patient profile
│   │   ├── timeline.ts       # 20+ realistic health events (2000–2025)
│   │   ├── family.ts         # Family member profiles
│   │   └── doctors.ts        # Mock HPR doctor profiles
│   ├── store/                # Zustand global state
│   │   ├── authStore.ts
│   │   ├── timelineStore.ts
│   │   └── languageStore.ts
│   └── i18n/
│       ├── en.ts
│       └── hi.ts             # Hindi translations
├── public/
│   └── icons/, fonts/
├── .env.example
├── vite.config.ts
├── tailwind.config.ts
└── package.json
```

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1 – Project Bootstrap

#### [NEW] `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`
- Vite 6 + React 19 + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first config)
- Dependencies: `react-router-dom` v7, `zustand`, `react-dropzone`, `qrcode.react`, `date-fns`, `@google/genai` ≥ 2.3.0, `lucide-react`, `framer-motion`

---

### 2 – Mock Data Layer (`src/mock/`)

#### [NEW] `patient.ts`
Realistic ABHA patient: Ramesh Kumar, ABHA `98-1234-5678-9012`, blood group O+, allergies (Penicillin, Sulfa drugs), chronic: Type 2 Diabetes (2015), Hypertension (2018).

#### [NEW] `timeline.ts`
25 realistic health events spanning 2000–2026 covering: childhood illnesses, acute events (typhoid, dengue), chronic management, surgeries, vaccinations. Each record has: `id`, `date`, `type` (illness/vaccination/surgery/checkup), `condition`, `doctor`, `hospital`, `medicines[]`, `dose`, `duration`, `outcome`, `source` (abdm|manual|uploaded).

#### [NEW] `family.ts`
3 family members: spouse, child (with vaccination schedule), elderly parent.

#### [NEW] `doctors.ts`
Mock HPR-verified doctors with specialisation, registration number.

---

### 3 – State Management (`src/store/`)

#### [NEW] `authStore.ts`
- `user`: current logged-in user (patient/doctor/family)
- `role`: `'patient' | 'doctor' | 'family'`
- `mockLogin(abhaNumber, otp)` → validates against mock data, sets user
- `logout()`

#### [NEW] `timelineStore.ts`
- `records[]`: all health records
- `filters`: year range, condition, doctor
- `addRecord(record)`, `mergeABDMRecords()`
- `recurringAlerts`: computed from records (same-condition within 2 years)

#### [NEW] `languageStore.ts`
- `lang: 'en' | 'hi'`
- `t(key)`: returns translated string

---

### 4 – i18n (`src/i18n/`)

#### [NEW] `en.ts` and `hi.ts`
Full translation coverage for all UI strings: navigation, buttons, labels, error messages, date formats.

---

### 5 – Pages

#### [NEW] `Landing.tsx`
Hero section: "Your health story, lifelong and yours" + ABHA logo integration badge. Features grid (Timeline, Digitiser, Emergency Card). Trust indicators (DPDP 2023, ABDM-compatible). CTA → Login.

#### [NEW] `Login.tsx`
Three tabs:
1. **Patient** – ABHA number/address + mock OTP flow (6-digit, auto-advance)
2. **Doctor** – HPR ID + OTP
3. **Family** – patient login with "Manage family" option
Mock ABHA login clearly labelled. Integration point comment for real ABDM OTP API.

#### [NEW] `Dashboard.tsx`
- Quick-stats bar: last visit, active medicines, upcoming reminders
- Recurring illness alert banner (if any)
- ABDM Sync button → shows merge animation → adds 3 mock ABDM records
- Recent timeline preview (last 5 records)
- Quick actions: Upload Record, Share Access, Emergency Card, Family

#### [NEW] `Timeline.tsx`
- Vertical timeline, grouped by year
- Each card: date, condition, doctor, hospital, medicines+dose+duration, outcome badge, source chip (ABDM/Uploaded/Manual)
- Filter sidebar: year range slider, condition multi-select, doctor filter, type checkboxes
- Search bar
- Recurring-illness chips linking past events
- Empty state with upload CTA

#### [NEW] `UploadReview.tsx`
**The main differentiator:**
1. Drop zone (photo or PDF, up to 10MB)
2. Image preview with zoom
3. "Extract with AI" button → calls Gemini Vision API with structured output prompt
4. Loading state with progress animation
5. Review form (pre-filled from OCR): date picker, doctor, hospital, condition, medicines table (name + dose + duration), notes
6. Diff highlighting: AI-extracted values shown in teal, user-edited values in amber
7. Confirm & Save → appends to timeline

#### [NEW] `DoctorSummary.tsx`
One-screen scannable view (intended for clinic use on patient's phone):
- Allergies (red badges)
- Chronic conditions (orange badges)
- Current medicines (table: name, dose, frequency)
- Past similar illnesses (last 3, with treatment that worked)
- Blood group + emergency contacts
- Print-friendly CSS

#### [NEW] `ShareAccess.tsx`
- "Generate Code" → creates 6-digit alphanumeric + QR code
- Timer countdown (24h by default, adjustable 1h/6h/24h)
- Revoke button
- Audit log table: who, when, what action, IP-like mock identifier
- Doctor view (when logged in as doctor): enter code → see patient's Doctor Summary

#### [NEW] `Family.tsx`
- Family member cards with mini health summary
- Add member modal (name, DOB, relation, ABHA optional)
- Child vaccination tracker: colorful schedule grid (BCG, OPV, DPT, MMR, etc.) with due/done/overdue status
- Reminder settings per member

#### [NEW] `EmergencyCard.tsx`
- Public-facing, no login: `/emergency/:token`
- Blood group (large), allergies, chronic conditions, emergency contacts, ABHA QR
- High-contrast teal/white, large text, suitable for unconscious patient scenario
- Generate Emergency Card button from Dashboard → creates shareable link + QR

---

### 6 – Core Components

#### [NEW] `components/timeline/TimelineCard.tsx`
Expandable card with source badge, condition chip, medicines list, outcome indicator.

#### [NEW] `components/timeline/IllnessAlert.tsx`
Banner: "⚠ You had similar symptoms in 2019 – treated with Azithromycin 500mg for 5 days."

#### [NEW] `components/upload/OCRReview.tsx`
Side-by-side: original image (pan/zoom) + extracted fields form.

#### [NEW] `components/consent/QRModal.tsx`
Full-screen modal with QR code, countdown timer, code display, revoke button.

#### [NEW] `components/family/VaccineTracker.tsx`
Grid of vaccine milestones for child profiles.

#### [NEW] `components/ui/`
Button, Badge, Modal, LanguageToggle, LoadingSpinner, EmptyState, Toast notification system.

---

### 7 – AI OCR Layer (`src/lib/gemini.ts`)

Calls `gemini-3.8-flash` with a structured output prompt + image/PDF as inline data. Returns:
```typescript
interface ExtractedRecord {
  date: string;           // YYYY-MM-DD
  doctorName: string;
  hospitalClinic: string;
  diagnosis: string;
  medicines: Array<{name: string; dose: string; duration: string}>;
  notes: string;
  confidence: number;     // 0–1
}
```
Falls back to mock extracted data if `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY` is not set.

---

### 8 – ABDM Stubs (`src/lib/abdm.ts`)

```typescript
// ABDM_INTEGRATION_POINT: Replace with real ABDM Health Records API call
export async function fetchABDMRecords(abhaNumber: string): Promise<HealthRecord[]>

// ABDM_INTEGRATION_POINT: Replace with real ABHA OTP verification
export async function verifyABHAOTP(abhaNumber: string, otp: string): Promise<AuthToken>
```

Mock returns 3 FHIR-shaped records after 1.5s delay.

---

### 9 – QR Layer (`src/lib/qr.ts`)
Generates consent codes (6-char alphanumeric + expiry) and emergency card tokens. Uses `qrcode.react` for rendering.

---

## Design System

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary | Teal `#0D9488` (teal-600) |
| Surface | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Muted | `#F0FDFA` (teal-50) |
| Text | `#134E4A` (teal-900) |
| Warning | `#D97706` (amber-600) |
| Danger | `#DC2626` (red-600) |
| Font | Inter (body), size base 16px, line-height 1.6 |
| Border radius | 12px cards, 8px inputs |
| Minimum tap target | 44×44px |

All interactive elements pass WCAG AA contrast. Large-text mode toggle bumps base font to 20px.

---

## Verification Plan

### Build & Lint
```bash
cd C:\Users\Lenovo\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\lifechart
npm run build
npm run lint
```

### Manual Smoke Test (all pages)
1. Landing → Login (patient mock OTP) → Dashboard
2. Dashboard → Timeline → filter by year/condition
3. Dashboard → Upload → drop an image → AI extract → review → save → verify in Timeline
4. Dashboard → Share Access → generate QR → copy code
5. Dashboard → Doctor Summary → verify scannable layout
6. Dashboard → Family → add member → view vaccination tracker
7. `/emergency/:token` → verify no-login emergency card
8. Language toggle (EN ↔ HI) on every page

<USER_REQUEST>
Build a responsive web app called "LifeChart" – a patient-friendly lifelong health timeline for India, built as a layer on top of India's ABDM/ABHA ecosystem (not a replacement for it).

POSITIONING
ABDM already provides ABHA IDs and consent-based record exchange. LifeChart adds what it lacks: digitising OLD paper records, a simple Hindi/English timeline, and instant doctor summaries.

USERS
1. Patient: login with ABHA number/address + OTP (demo mode: mock ABHA and mock OTP, with clearly marked integration points for real ABDM APIs later).
2. Doctor: verified via Healthcare Professionals Registry ID (mock for now). Sees a record only after patient consent.
3. Family manager: one account manages parents, children and elderly relatives.

CORE FEATURES
1. Old Records Digitiser (main differentiator): upload photos/PDFs of old prescriptions and reports. OCR extracts doctor, date, diagnosis, medicines, dose, duration. User reviews and confirms the extracted data before saving.
2. Lifelong Health Timeline: birth to today, filterable by year, condition, doctor. Shows illness, treatment given, dose, days to recover.
3. ABDM Sync: "Fetch my ABDM records" button that merges government-linked records into the same timeline (mock data for now).
4. Doctor Quick Summary (one screen): allergies, chronic conditions, current medicines, past similar illnesses, and what treatment worked before. Simple, scannable, no clutter.
5. Consent Sharing: patient generates a QR/6-digit code at the clinic. Doctor gets time-limited access (24h), read plus add only. Patient can revoke anytime. Full audit log of who viewed what.
6. Recurring-Illness Alert: "You had a similar condition in 2019 – treated with X for 5 days."
7. Family and Vaccination: child profiles, vaccination schedule tracker, reminders.
8. Emergency Card: QR showing blood group, allergies, emergency contacts, no login needed.
9. Medicine and follow-up reminders.
10. Hindi/English toggle, plus voice input for adding records.

SECURITY
Encryption in transit and at rest, explicit consent for every share, minimal data collection, DPDP Act 2023-aligned. Never store Aadhaar numbers.

UI/UX
Trustworthy medical look (teal and white), large text, mobile-first, elderly-friendly. Pages: Landing, Login, Dashboard, Timeline, Upload and Review, Doctor Summary, Share Access, Family, Emergency Card.

TECH
React + Tailwind frontend, Supabase (PostgreSQL, storage, auth) backend. Start with a fully working frontend using realistic mock data, then add real OCR and ABDM sandbox integration.
</USER_REQUEST>

<USER_REQUEST>
Build a responsive web app called "LifeChart" – a patient-friendly lifelong health timeline for India, built as a layer on top of India's ABDM/ABHA ecosystem (not a replacement for it).

POSITIONING
ABDM already provides ABHA IDs and consent-based record exchange. LifeChart adds what it lacks: digitising OLD paper records, a simple Hindi/English timeline, and instant doctor summaries.

USERS
1. Patient: login with ABHA number/address + OTP (demo mode: mock ABHA and mock OTP, with clearly marked integration points for real ABDM APIs later).
2. Doctor: verified via Healthcare Professionals Registry ID (mock for now). Sees a record only after patient consent.
3. Family manager: one account manages parents, children and elderly relatives.

CORE FEATURES
1. Old Records Digitiser (main differentiator): upload photos/PDFs of old prescriptions and reports. OCR extracts doctor, date, diagnosis, medicines, dose, duration. User reviews and confirms the extracted data before saving.
2. Lifelong Health Timeline: birth to today, filterable by year, condition, doctor. Shows illness, treatment given, dose, days to recover.
3. ABDM Sync: "Fetch my ABDM records" button that merges government-linked records into the same timeline (mock data for now).
4. Doctor Quick Summary (one screen): allergies, chronic conditions, current medicines, past similar illnesses, and what treatment worked before. Simple, scannable, no clutter.
5. Consent Sharing: patient generates a QR/6-digit code at the clinic. Doctor gets time-limited access (24h), read plus add only. Patient can revoke anytime. Full audit log of who viewed what.
6. Recurring-Illness Alert: "You had a similar condition in 2019 – treated with X for 5 days."
7. Family and Vaccination: child profiles, vaccination schedule tracker, reminders.
8. Emergency Card: QR showing blood group, allergies, emergency contacts, no login needed.
9. Medicine and follow-up reminders.
10. Hindi/English toggle, plus voice input for adding records.

SECURITY
Encryption in transit and at rest, explicit consent for every share, minimal data collection, DPDP Act 2023-aligned. Never store Aadhaar numbers.

UI/UX
Trustworthy medical look (teal and white), large text, mobile-first, elderly-friendly. Pages: Landing, Login, Dashboard, Timeline, Upload and Review, Doctor Summary, Share Access, Family, Emergency Card.

TECH
React + Tailwind frontend, Supabase (PostgreSQL, storage, auth) backend. Start with a fully working frontend using realistic mock data, then add real OCR and ABDM sandbox integration.
</USER_REQUEST>
